subject.title: [security] Azure deferred cleanup deletes by resource name without ownership re-verification

question: Should Azure deferred cleanup fail closed unless a live provider read-back proves the target resources still belong to the exact Crabbox lease before deletion?
rationale: The source-supported gap crosses the documented destructive provider ownership boundary, but changing the timeout cleanup path to fail closed can affect operator cleanup and recovery behavior for stale or partial Azure resources.

options.title: Harden deferred cleanup fail-closed
options.body: Persist lease and expected ownership context, require live Azure ownership verification before deleting, and keep retry or diagnostic state when proof is missing.

options.title: Retire suspicious records without deletion
options.body: Treat missing or mismatched ownership as an operator-review condition and clear or quarantine records only after explicit maintainer-approved diagnostics.

options.title: Accept name-only retry cleanup
options.body: Keep the current cleanup behavior and accept that the alarm path trusts the stored generated name as sufficient destructive authority.

recommendation.title: Harden deferred cleanup fail-closed
recommendation.body: Persist lease and expected ownership context, require live Azure ownership verification before deleting, and keep retry or diagnostic state when proof is missing.
